newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-INJURED O'BRIEN PULLS OUT OF U.S. CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-INJURED O'BRIEN PULLS OUT OF U.S. CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: World decathlon record-holder Dan O'Brien said on Wednesday he would not compete in next week's U.S. championships because of an apparent stress fracture.
The withdrawal means both O'Brien, the three-time world champion and Olympic gold medalist, and world 200-meter record-holder Michael Johnson likely will miss August's world championships in Athens.

Only athletes who compete in the U.S. championships are eligible for the American team, and Johnson's coach said Tuesday that it is highly unlikely the double Olympic champion would participate in the U.S. meet June 11-15 at Indianapolis because of an injury he suffered in his 150-meter match race with Canadian Donovan Bailey.
"It's just bad timing. It is going to take three or four weeks for this to go away," O'Brien said of the injury to his right tibia.
He said both he and Johnson are likely to petition U.S. officials to be allowed to compete in the world championships.

"What happens if Dan O'Brien and Michael Johnson don't make the world championship team," O'Brien said in an interview at the U.S. collegiate championships. "How's that going to make the selection committee look?"
"There should be exemptions for people who deserve them," O'Brien said. "We're the only country in the world still that demands their athletes compete to qualify.

"I think the IAAF should pick athletes (for the world championships) and everybody picked by the IAAF should have the ability to go. If there are eight Kenyans in the steeplechase, so what? They are the best in the world."
But a U.S. track and field spokesman said only those who finish in the top three at the U.S. championships are eligible for the world team.
O'Brien said that if he does not compete in the world meet, he probably "would not do anything this summer, just rest."

"My main goal is to win again in 2000," he said, referring to the Sydney Games. "But somewhere along the line I'm going to have to take some time off. I've trained for six years in a row. I'm a little bit tired, but I think I could put it all together and come up big at the world championships."
The injury, he said, is similar to one he experienced in 1992, when he did not make the U.S. Olympic team after failing to clear a height in the pole vault.
"I think I just pressed in my training in the spring," he said. "It definitely held me back from training for the last month."
